LESSON: CONSERVING WILD ANIMALS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Conservation of Resources
Topic 1.4: Conserving Wild Animals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Conserving Wild Animals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we scare off small wild animals from crop enterprises?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify small wild animals that destroy crops
2. construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONSERVING WILD ANIMALS
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Conserving Wild Animals helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT ANIMALS
Animals are living things. They move, feed, grow, and respond to their surroundings.
Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).
Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).
In Kenya you may see cows in a homestead, fish at a market, or birds on the school field.
Safety: do not touch unknown animals; wash hands after handling pets or farm animals.

PART 1: Identify small wild animals that destroy crops

What this means
In this part you learn to identify small wild animals that destroy crops. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify small wild animals that destroy crops.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Conserving Wild Animals” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify small wild animals that destroy crops. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops

What this means
In this part you learn to construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Conserving Wild Animals matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Conserving Wild Animals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Domestic animals live with people (cow, goat, chicken, dog, cat).

Wild animals live on their own in forests, parks, or water (lion, zebra, fish).

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Conserving Wild Animals” around your school. (skill: identify small wild animals that destroy crops)

Example 2: Say why Conserving Wild Animals matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Conserving Wild Animals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify small wild animals that destroy crops.
3. Practise this skill: construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Conserving Wild Animals from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Conserving Wild Animals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Conserving Wild Animals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we scare off small wild animals from crop enterprises?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Conserving Wild Animals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify small wild animals that destroy crops.
5. Be able to: construct and use a scarecrow to scare off small wild animals from crops.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
